      If a thick closure contains both terms as degree-zero stalks, it contains the complex of any differential between those terms.

      ∃ (B : TwoTerm R), have T := U.directSum B; T.IsPresilting ∧ T.InThick (inDegreeZero G) ∧ ∀ (Y : TwoTerm R), Function.Surjective ⇑(U.homotopyBoundary Y) → Function.Surjective ⇑(T.homotopyBoundary Y)

      Completing U at a finite projective G gives a presilting complex containing U, generating the stalk of G, and preserving every right orthogonality of U.

      A finite projective stalk belongs to the thick closure of any two-term complex that generates the regular stalk.

      theorem EFiniteCharacterizations.TwoTerm.exists_bongartz_generator {R : Type u} [Ring R] [IsNoetherianRing R] (k : Type u) [Field k] [Algebra k R] [Module.Finite k R] (U : TwoTerm R) (hu : U.IsPresilting) :
      ∃ (B : TwoTerm R), have T := U.directSum B; T.IsPresilting ∧ (∀ (X : TwoTerm R), T.InThick X) ∧ ∀ (Y : TwoTerm R), Function.Surjective ⇑(U.homotopyBoundary Y) → Function.Surjective ⇑(T.homotopyBoundary Y)

      The Bongartz completion is a silting generator on two-term projectives and preserves the positive right orthogonality of the original complex.
